title: Session-anchored Canary with Traffic Lease Tokens and Rewind Rollback
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Session affinity during canary rollouts causes noisy user experiences when in-flight sessions are cut over to a new model mid-conversation. This PR implements a session-anchored canary primitive that issues short-lived traffic lease tokens to keep ongoing sessions pinned to the original model until a safe handoff point, and adds a deterministic "rewind" rollback mechanism that can replay pinned sessions against a previous model for stateful reconciliation.

What this PR introduces: 1) Traffic Lease Tokens: new lightweight token that the gateway attaches to session-level requests. Tokens are acquired by the node that handles the first request in a session and are enforced by the routing layer for the token's TTL. 2) Handshake + Handoff API: a control-plane API for creating handoff windows so a session can finish a bounded number of turns before being moved. 3) Checkpointed Session Snapshots: at handoff points we persist a compact session checkpoint (KV of conversation pointers and short-term model KV-cache metadata) to the rollout store. 4) Rewind Rollback: when an automated rollback is triggered, the system can replay the checkpointed session against the target model (previous version) and emit reconciliation events and metrics. 5) Safety locks and draining semantics: explicit safety lock prevents model swap until all critical leases are released or max-handshake-timeouts elapse. 6) Observability and playbooks: new metrics, dashboards, and a runbook for operators.

Implementation notes: - Control plane: rollout service gains endpoints /lease/acquire, /lease/release, /handoff/start, /rewind/replay. These are backward-compatible (old gateways ignore lease headers). - Data model: added rollout.leases table (lease_id, session_id, owner_node, ttl, created_at) and session_checkpoints (checkpoint_id, session_id, snapshot_blob, created_at). TTLs are configurable per-deployment. - Routing: router now respects X-Session-Lease header; if absent behavior is identical to current fallback routing. - Performance: lease check is cached in-memory per-router to avoid DB roundtrips on every token check; we added a small consistent-hash lookup path for lease ownership. - Tests: unit tests for lease lifecycle, integration tests for handoff/during-canary, e2e playback test that verifies fidelity of rewind replay.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc (links/ENG-7412) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] e2e replay test - [x] Observability dashboards - [x] Docs + runbook - [x] Backwards compatibility validation

Risk & Mitigations: The primary risk is lease ownership divergence under transient partitions. Mitigations: (a) conservative TTL defaults (30s), (b) fail-open routing when local lease cache cannot be validated and request is tagged non-critical, (c) automatic lease reconciliation job.

How to test locally: - run ./dev/rollout up - run ./dev/gateway with --enable-session-lease - run tests/integration/test_handoff.py

Related work: This PR complements the existing shadow/replica frameworks (see ENG-6021) and ties into the rollout contracts added in ENG-6993.

Summary: Adds session-anchored canary behavior to reduce user-visible flakiness during model swaps and provides a deterministic rollback "rewind" to reconcile long-running sessions on rollback.

release_notes: Session-anchored canaries: introduce short-lived traffic lease tokens to pin in-flight sessions during model rollouts. Added rewind rollback to deterministically replay session checkpoints against previous model versions. New DB tables rollout.leases and session_checkpoints. Backwards compatible routing when tokens absent. Operators: see docs/rollouts/session-lease.md for runbook and Grafana dashboard.
summary: Implements session-level lease tokens to maintain session affinity across canary rollouts, plus a checkpoint-and-replay rollback to reconcile long-running sessions on rollback.
